neighbours.label: the perfect auxiliary 'has/have/'ve' opening a present-perfect verb, strongest before 'been' ('has been diagnosed', 'they've been working'), as against the simple past of the same verb
fire: Since the spring, my sister has been teaching piano at the school.
The neighbors say they've been hearing strange noises at night.
For three years now, the mayor has been fighting the new highway.
Our team has been training twice a day before the final.
Lately the kids have been building a treehouse in the yard.
The old bridge has been closed for repairs since March.
My parents say they've been saving for a new kitchen.
Doctors report the patient has been responding well to treatment.
